summary: Milo sits on a low crate in the lower deck of the tanker, struggling to thread a thick copper wire through a series of ceramic insulators while the floor vibrates from a distant sandstorm. Lucia stands over him, her hand resting on the hilt of a ceramic blade tucked into her belt as she watches his grease-stained fingers fumble with the delicate electronics. She leans down and purposefully kicks a small box of essential mounting brackets under a heavy coolant tank, her eyes remaining fixed on Milo to see if he notices the deliberate movement. Milo pauses, his brow furrowing as he looks around the cluttered floor for the missing components, unaware that Lucia has already replaced them with unstable, high-velocity ignition caps. Lucia smiles thinly, her expression hidden in the shadows of the engine room as she watches him reach for the compromised hardware. "The parts you're looking for won't help you build a radio, but they'll certainly make that bird fly faster."
settingText: Mojave Launch-Shop field site — bright open-desert workspace with maintained legacy aerospace equipment, organized tools, practical rigging and dramatic geological distance.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: Those parts will not improve the radio. They will improve range and survivability. Decide whether that serves this mission.

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: What happens when pursuit becomes identity?

dialogueInline.speaker: Cyrus
dialogueInline.text: You stop noticing whether the target still justifies it.

summary: Arvin stands at the base of a towering, patchwork rocket made of corrugated iron and scavenged turbine blades, his hand pressed firmly against the vibrating hull. Milo crouches near the ignition lead, his hands trembling as he prepares to touch the live wires together while the wind howls across the cracked surface of the dry lake bed. The sun hangs low on the horizon, painting the scene in deep oranges and long, dramatic shadows that stretch toward the dust clouds of approaching Tethergrid interceptors. Arvin nods slowly, his eyes locked on Milo, signaling the start of a countdown that relies more on physical instinct than any digital clock. Milo grips the copper leads, his knuckles white, waiting for the precise moment the pressure gauge hits the red line marked in permanent marker. "Let it go now, before the heat of the core fuses your fingers to the frame."
settingText: Mojave limestone cave — cool pale mineral interior, practical portable worklights, rough stone and equipment carried in from the bright desert.

dialogueInline.speaker: Milo
dialogueInline.text: The core is heating your gloves. Let go now, Arv. We can rebuild the frame.

dialogueInline.speaker: Lucia
dialogueInline.text: What do you think he sees when he looks at us?

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: A technical problem he expected to solve without learning our names.

dialogueInline.speaker: Arvin
dialogueInline.text: Now he knows the faces. That makes simple answers harder.
